{"id":"persona-5s4b.15","title":"AttestorError variants carry opaque Strings; callers cannot distinguish user-cancel from device-absent","description":"persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:88-97. `AttestorError` has three variants: `Unavailable(String)`, `ChallengeFailed(String)`, `Io(std::io::Error)`. The doc on `prove()` (lib.rs:122-124) states ChallengeFailed covers both "the user cancels" and "the hardware key is not present" — two cases that demand opposite caller responses: user-cancel means stop and surface a message, device-absent means fall back to the next attestor.

With the current shape the only way to tell them apart is substring-matching the String, which is not a contract and differs per attestor. persona-grpc/src/service.rs:133-136 shows the consequence at the one real call site today: every enumerate error is collapsed to a warn log and the attestor silently skipped, because there is nothing to branch on.

Same issue for `Unavailable(String)`, which is used both for "SSH_AUTH_SOCK not set" (ssh.rs:88, a permanent condition) and "cannot connect to SSH agent" (ssh.rs:92, transient), and for oidc.rs:179 "no cached token found for this claim", which is really a wrong-claim error, not an availability error.

The enum is already `#[non_exhaustive]`, so adding structured variants (UserCancelled, DeviceAbsent, Timeout, UnknownClaim, NotConfigured) is a non-breaking change now and stays cheap only until downstream code starts matching on the current three.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:57:28.626061775Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:57:28.626061775Z","labels":["risk","api-contract","defensive","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.15","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:57:28.65118926Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}
